en.name: Gochugaru
en.summary: Once opened, gochugaru holds its full colour and aroma for about 6 months in an airtight, opaque container in a cool cupboard. It stays safe well beyond that — it simply fades to a dull brown-orange. Korean households commonly keep it cold, which slows the fading further; just let the container reach room temperature before opening it, so condensation stays off the powder.
en.pantry: About 6 months after opening, the same as any other ground spice — gochugaru is ground chilli, and it fades the way ground spices do. Airtight, opaque container, away from the cooker. For an unopened bag, go by the date the maker prints on it. What you are protecting is the colour and the fruity aroma that distinguishes good gochugaru from generic chilli powder; heat, light and air take all three.
en.fridge: Korean households routinely keep 고춧가루 in the fridge, and in a humid climate that is the sensible choice: it holds the red colour, keeps the powder free-running and shuts out pantry moths. No agency publishes a cold-storage timeline for it, so no number is given here — inventing one would be worse than saying so. Let a cold bag come fully to room temperature before you open it, or condensation will cake the powder.
en.freezer: Same reasoning as the fridge. Freezing preserves colour and pungency indefinitely for practical purposes, and it is what many Korean cooks actually do with a large bag, but there is no published home figure to quote. Double-bag it and portion it so you are not thawing the whole bag every time you make kimchi or a stew. Again, open the bag only after it has warmed to room temperature.
en.thawing: Let the sealed bag reach room temperature before opening, so condensation forms on the bag rather than on the powder. Do not thaw and refreeze repeatedly.
spoilage: A dull brown-orange colour where the flakes were bright red.
Little or no fruity aroma when you warm a pinch in your palm.
Caking into lumps, which means moisture has got in.
Mould inside a damp lump, which means the bag goes.
tips: Store in an opaque airtight container; light bleaches chilli faster than heat does.
Portion a large bag before freezing so you open only what you need.
Let cold gochugaru warm up sealed before opening it.
Coarse flakes for kimchi, fine powder for stews and sauces — keep them separately labelled.

faq.a: About 6 months after opening in an airtight, opaque container in a cool cupboard, for full colour and aroma. It stays safe longer than that; it just fades.

faq.q: Should gochugaru be kept in the fridge or freezer?
faq.a: In a humid climate, yes — it keeps the colour and shuts out moths. No agency publishes a cold-storage timeline for it, so no number is given here.

faq.q: My gochugaru has gone brown. Is it bad?
faq.a: It is faded, not unsafe. Light and air have bleached the pigment. Use it in a cooked stew where colour matters less, and buy smaller amounts next time.

zh.name: 韓式辣椒粉
zh.summary: 開封之後，韓式辣椒粉裝在不透光的氣密容器、放在陰涼櫥櫃，大約 6 個月內能維持完整的顏色與香氣。超過之後它仍然是安全的——只是會褪成暗淡的褐橘色。韓國家庭普遍會把它冰起來，那確實能讓褪色更慢；只是要用之前請讓容器回到室溫再打開，免得結露落在粉上。
zh.pantry: 開封後大約 6 個月，和其他研磨香料一樣——它就是磨碎的辣椒，走味的方式也一樣。請用不透光的氣密容器，遠離爐具。未開封的袋子請以製造商標示的日期為準。你要保護的，是顏色，以及讓好的韓式辣椒粉有別於一般辣椒粉的那股果香；而溫度、光線和空氣會把這三樣一起帶走。
zh.fridge: 韓國家庭本來就習慣把고춧가루放冰箱，在潮濕的氣候下這也是合理的選擇：顏色保得住、粉不會結塊，也擋掉穀蛾。但沒有機關公布它的低溫保存期限，所以這裡不給數字——硬編一個會比誠實說沒有更糟。冰過的袋子請完全回到室溫再打開，否則結露會把粉弄結塊。
zh.freezer: 理由和冷藏一樣。就實務而言，冷凍可以幾乎無限期保住顏色與辣度，很多韓國廚房對大包裝也真的這麼做；但沒有可以引用的家用數字。請雙層裝袋並分裝，免得每次做泡菜或燉湯都要解凍一整包。同樣地，要等回到室溫再開袋。
zh.thawing: 讓密封袋回到室溫再打開，讓結露留在袋子上而不是粉上。不要反覆解凍又冷凍。
spoilage: 原本鮮紅的辣椒片變成暗淡的褐橘色。
在手心搓熱一小撮，幾乎聞不到那股果香。
結成塊狀，代表水氣跑進去了。
受潮的硬塊裡看得到霉——那整包就該丟。
tips: 用不透光的氣密容器；光線漂白辣椒的速度比溫度還快。
大包裝先分裝再冷凍，每次只開需要的那一份。
冰過的辣椒粉要密封回溫後再打開。
粗片用來做泡菜、細粉用來煮湯和調醬，分開標示比較好用。

faq.q: 韓式辣椒粉可以放多久？
faq.a: 開封後用不透光氣密容器放陰涼櫥櫃，大約 6 個月能維持完整的顏色與香氣。之後仍然安全，只是會退色。

faq.q: 韓式辣椒粉要冷藏或冷凍嗎？
faq.a: 在潮濕氣候下值得——顏色保得住，也擋掉穀蛾。但沒有機關公布低溫保存的期限，所以這裡不給數字。

faq.q: 辣椒粉變褐色了是壞掉嗎？
faq.a: 是退色，不是不安全。光線和空氣把色素漂淡了。拿去煮湯這種比較不看顏色的料理，下次買少一點。
